about: Ordinary next questions: what the CIO may write as synthesis.followUp and the check (api/_lib/desk-next-question.ts) must serve as written. Each row is [symbol, question]. scripts/test-desk-levels.mts runs every row through servedFollowUp.

How it was made: written by hand on 2026-10-08 by the engineer who then widened the word list (an AI model, Claude), as a CIO model would write them from the live prompt (NEXT_QUESTION_RULE and the followUp description in api/_lib/desk-debate.ts): one question, what or why, about the asset by its ticker or its name, at most 12 words, no number. No model was called: this is not real model output.

languages (the blind sample, 183 to 197 per language): every question was written, counted and frozen before its author read api/_lib/desk-next-question-lexicon.ts or the body of the check; only the prompt sentence, the function signatures and the list of supported symbols had been read. Nothing was added, removed or reworded afterwards to make a question pass. Served as written before the second pass: 32% to 47% per language (firstPass.languages).

later (70 or 71 per language): two more batches, each written after the list had been widened for the one before and measured once before the list was widened for it. Their first measurement is what a question nobody has seen met at that moment (firstPass.second, firstPass.third). Their author had read the list by then, and varied the wording on purpose.

holdout (20 per language): a fourth batch, measured once and left alone. The list was NOT widened for it. It is the yardstick, not a target: what an ordinary question in words nobody listed meets today (firstPass.holdout). The test prints its rate and only requires that it does not fall.

What is in the questions on purpose: analyst vocabulary (price action, technicals, catalysts, sentiment, timeframes, consolidation, divergence, breakout, pullback, volume, moving averages, funding, open interest, earnings, guidance, sector, macro), hedged phrasing, possessives, hyphenated words, borrowed English terms in the other five languages, stocks, crypto, exchange-qualified tickers (MC.PA, PETR4.SA, 7203.T) and a company name in place of the ticker.

What is not in them: any question about acting, owning, timing an entry or an exit, a forecast, a price or a person. A few carry a word the check refuses for a reason (gaining, rendimientos, the best way to, another asset's ticker, add, dejar): they were written before the list was read, they stay, and they are the refusals that remain.

Typography, applied by rule when the lists were assembled (a model writes either form): every fifth question with an apostrophe carries the typographic one; in French the space before the question mark is a plain space, a no-break space (every fourth, from the second), a narrow no-break space (every fourth, from the fourth) or none (every sixth).

Limits: the six lists of each batch share their themes, so they are less varied than six independent samples; the other five languages were not reviewed by a native speaker; and the measured rates say how the check treats these questions, not how it treats what the production models write.
